grh_fa6a7061c99c65900b2f.title: The Duke of Nevers
paragraphs: In 1885 San Francisco, wealthy Harry Penrod is alarmed when his daughter Gertie returns from Europe married to Charles Jules Francois, a penniless Frenchman who calls himself the Duke de Nevers and commander of the Legion of Honor. Charles lives by an elaborate code of aristocratic honor, refuses an offered business partnership and never touches a large sum Mrs. Penrod places within his reach. His downfall comes when he tries to help a young couple by pledging property he does not own as bail, leading to his arrest for false statements and fraud. Investigation shows the historic Nevers line has been extinct for generations, and Charles privately admits to Gertie that he was born poor in Paris and married her under false pretenses. Sentenced to five years at hard labor, he nevertheless refuses to abandon the noble identity he has created for himself, insisting to the end that he is the Duke de Nevers.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on April 16, 1979. It is listed as episode 51 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Anne Gibbon, Fletcher Markle, Howard Culver, Len Birman, and Vic Perrin. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Percy Grainger as writer, and Lorne Greene as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_fab10673dc2f9a4593d1.title: The Wonderful One-Hoss Shay
paragraphs: Across generations, a New England family boasts of the 'perfect' one-hoss shay built so every piece is exactly as strong as every other. A young minister inherits both the carriage and the family's faith in perfection, even letting that attitude interfere with his courtship of Nell; on the shay's hundredth birthday every part gives way at once, humbling him and teaching that neither machines nor people can be made flawless before he returns to Nell with a more modest outlook.

grh_fa0a7374a3e46c415a45.title: The Hard Way
paragraphs: Trying to go straight, Harry accepts $1,000 to fly a wealthy man's troublesome young niece to a finishing school in Switzerland. The girl secretly turns the trip into a kidnapping scheme of her own, hoping Harry will demand a huge ransom from her uncle so she can take the money and marry her fiancé. Harry wants no part of the plan and lands at the remote farm of his old associate Mo while deciding what to do. Mo mistakes the situation for a real abduction and is horrified that Harry has broken his promise to stay legitimate. Harry returns the girl to her uncle, who is determined to get her safely to school. The episode ends with one final complication: during her stay at the farm she stole $60,000 of counterfeit money from Mo.

grh_fae421a0a809f37bdf39.title: The Fifth of November
paragraphs: James Stewart tells Holmes that his cousin Falconbridge is plotting against him amid Guy Fawkes Day tunnels, gunpowder and disguises. Holmes discovers Stewart himself rented the neighboring house, planted the supposed conspiracy clues and tried to build a case that Falconbridge meant to kill him, so that Stewart could shoot his cousin and claim self-defense. The scheme collapses when Holmes substitutes an unloaded revolver and exposes the planted dagger; Stewart flees across the rooftops carrying a Guy Fawkes dummy and dies after the strain and excitement overwhelm him.

This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.6c28d2e9a5bfb8b6|The Adventure of the Devil's Foot]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_fa1d3323f5050c029dc3.title: The Lovers
paragraphs: Rough frontiersman Simon Guthrie returns to town and eventually marries Eve Mitchell, who begins teaching him to read and write while they build a future together. Their new life is threatened when the jealous Ward Hutton arrives armed and Eve is shot during the confrontation. Ward is jailed, but Eve's blood loss and later pneumonia leave her close to death while Simon keeps working on the house they planned. She survives, and the story closes with Simon bringing her to the finished home and the two rocking chairs waiting on its porch.

grh_fae2e19fff17e06387cd.title: Battle Report-Pearl Harbor to the Coral Sea
paragraphs: A dramatization from Battle Report personifies the submarine tender USS Canopus as she recounts her role in the doomed defense of Bataan and Corregidor. Damaged but still operating, the ship is disguised to appear destroyed while her repair facilities support the fighting, and members of her crew later serve ashore as improvised infantry. When Bataan falls, the crew takes Canopus into deep water and scuttles her rather than surrender the ship, while the closing narration promises that the Navy will preserve her name in a new vessel.
